target_customer: VR headset owners and web developers building WebVR content
problem: VR content lived in closed app stores; Supermedium offered a browser and space for web-based VR so any web VR content could be reached.
business_model: Free VR browser and utilities; monetization not established in sources

founders.name: Diego Marcos Segura
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; Road to VR and TechCrunch describe the team as Mozilla WebVR veterans who created A-Frame.

technical_complexity.rationale: A WebVR browser needs deep browser and graphics expertise; the team came from Mozilla's WebVR standards work.

defensibility.rationale: Free tooling on open web standards and dependent on headset makers; little to stop platforms from adding web VR.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: An aggregator headline says the VR browser is no longer in active development (undated); the company now publishes Abracadabra, a 3D generative AI workflow for A-Frame.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (July 2018) described walled VR stores as the alternative approach, and the browser did not support Oculus Go or Gear VR at the time.

branding.brand_signature: Link to A-Frame, the creators of A-Frame
branding.community_and_virality: Discord and Twitter links on the current site; the A-Frame community is an asset but sources do not tie it to the Supermedium name.

brand_strength.rationale: No sourced brand press; the team is known mainly through A-Frame.

pivots.from: VR browser and space of immersive utilities
pivots.to: Abracadabra generative AI 3D content creation for A-Frame
pivots.why: Not stated; the current site shows the new product with a 2024 copyright

outcome_analysis: Supermedium raised a 1.1 million dollar seed in July 2018 to build a WebVR browser, but the consumer VR market stayed small and walled stores dominated. An undated aggregator item says the browser is no longer actively developed, and the team now ships 3D generative AI tools, so the original idea stalled without a documented exit.
notes: Search results name Kevin Ngo and Diego Goberna as co-founders, but no opened source states it, so only Marcos is listed. Failure factors are my reading from sparse evidence; the cause of stall is not public. Aggregators list 1.22M over 3 rounds (CB Insights), unverified. Competitors: no named rival in the 2018 TechCrunch or Road to VR articles; list left empty. Branding facts are thin; unknown fields left null. Seed amounts match across TechCrunch and Road to VR (publication dates differ by two days).
